input: A defect-reduction project that was carried out on a moulding cell succeeded in cutting the reject rate from 2.9% to 1.2% over the course of one quarter, which represents a considerable improvement in the performance of the cell. When the improvement is expressed on an annual basis, at a production volume of 116k units per year the change corresponds to avoiding approximately 1972 rejected units per year, which gives a sense of the scale of the benefit that the project has delivered. The improvement was achieved across the whole of the quarter in which the project ran, and the annualised figure that follows from it is intended to give the reader a clearer sense of what the reduction in the reject rate amounts to when it is viewed at the scale of a full year of production. It should be noted, however, that the quarter in question included a planned shutdown, and the rates that are reported here have not been adjusted in order to take that shutdown into account, so a degree of caution should be exercised when the figures are interpreted and when they are compared with the performance of other periods.
target: A defect-reduction project on a moulding cell cut the reject rate from 2.9% to 1.2% over one quarter. At 116k units per year, the change avoids about 1972 rejected units per year. The quarter included a planned shutdown, and the rates are not adjusted for it. The comparison is therefore a comparison of rates over the production that ran: the shutdown reduced the output of the quarter without entering the rate figures, and the avoided-units figure is the annual volume carried at the stated rates, not a count of rejects avoided inside the quarter itself. The result stands as a rate result. The reject rate after the project is less than half the rate before it, on the production the quarter contained, and the annual figure states what that rate difference is worth at the stated volume. The rate figures themselves are the durable part of the result: volumes change with the programme of work, but a reject rate is a property of the cell as it now runs, and the reduction in that property is what the project is responsible for. The avoided-units figure translates that property into units for planning purposes. A quarter without a shutdown would test whether the new rate holds at full output, and that test has not yet been run.
